text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A top Kenyan criminal lawyer is shot dead by a lone gunman in Nairobi.
- Parliament authorises the withdrawal of 10.3 billion shillings ($1.9 million) from the Consolidated Fund to allow the government to fund the voter registration exercise by June.
- Ruling party grassroot elections in the Lake Victoria town of Kisumu are marred by violence.
- President Daniel arap Moi orders private developers to keep away from Nairobi's country bus station.
- A much-awaited independent report on the murder of British tourist Julie Ward will be released to the public by the end of the week.
- Twenty-three tourists in Kenya demand for compensation from Kenyan police after spending the weekend in police cells.
- President Moi to leave on Wednesday for a state visit to Zimbabwe.
- Two hundred members of opposition FORD-Asili party defect to the ruling party.
- Eight students from a secondary school in eastern Kenya drank contaminated water. ($1=54 Kenya Shillings)
